stem.en: This time next week, we ___ on a beach in Turkey.

why.en: An action in progress at a future moment: will be + -ing (will be lying).
why.uz: Kelajakdagi muayyan paytda davom etadigan harakat: will be + -ing (will be lying).
why.ru: Действие, которое будет длиться в определённый момент будущего: will be + -ing (will be lying).

why.en: By + a future time shows the action will be finished before then: will have + past participle.
why.uz: By + kelajakdagi vaqt harakat undan oldin tugashini bildiradi: will have + uchinchi shakl.
why.ru: By + время в будущем: действие завершится к этому моменту: will have + третья форма.

stem.en: ___ you be using your bike tomorrow? I'd like to borrow it.

why.en: Will + subject + be + -ing politely asks about someone's plans: Will you be using...?
why.uz: Will + ega + be + -ing kimningdir rejasi haqida xushmuomala soʻrash usuli: Will you be using...?
why.ru: Will + подлежащее + be + -ing — вежливый вопрос о планах: Will you be using...?

stem.en: By the end of this month, she ___ all her savings.

why.en: Finished before a future point: will have + past participle; will is never followed by has.
why.uz: Kelajakdagi nuqtagacha tugaydigan harakat: will have + uchinchi shakl; will dan keyin has kelmaydi.
why.ru: Действие завершится к моменту в будущем: will have + третья форма; после will не бывает has.

stem.en: ___ the heavy rain, the match continued.

why.en: Before a noun phrase (the heavy rain) we use despite; although and even though need a clause.
why.uz: Ot birikmasi oldidan (the heavy rain) despite ishlatiladi; although va even though dan keyin gap kerak.
why.ru: Перед именной группой (the heavy rain) — despite; после although и even though нужно придаточное.

stem.en: My sister loves maths, ___ I prefer languages.

why.en: Whereas joins two clauses that compare different facts.
why.uz: Whereas ikki xil faktni solishtiruvchi ikki gapni bogʻlaydi.
why.ru: Whereas соединяет два предложения, сопоставляя разные факты.

stem.en: In spite of ___ very tired, he went to the gym.

why.en: In spite of is followed by a noun or an -ing form: in spite of being tired.
why.uz: In spite of dan keyin ot yoki -ing shakli keladi: in spite of being tired.
why.ru: После in spite of идёт существительное или форма на -ing: in spite of being tired.

stem.en: The hotel was expensive. ___, we decided to stay there.

why.en: Nevertheless starts a new sentence and shows contrast with the one before.
why.uz: Nevertheless yangi gapni boshlaydi va oldingi gapga qarama-qarshilikni koʻrsatadi.
why.ru: Nevertheless начинает новое предложение и противопоставляет его предыдущему.

stem.en: ___ down the street, I saw an old friend.

why.en: A present participle (Walking) describes what the subject (I) was doing at the same time.
why.uz: Hozirgi zamon sifatdoshi (Walking) ega (I) bir vaqtning oʻzida nima qilayotganini bildiradi.
why.ru: Причастие настоящего времени (Walking) описывает, что подлежащее (I) делало в то же время.

stem.en: Most of the people ___ to the party were classmates.

why.en: The people were invited by someone, so we use the past participle: people invited (= who were invited).
why.uz: Odamlar kimdir tomonidan taklif qilingan, shuning uchun uchinchi shakl: people invited (= who were invited).
why.ru: Людей кто-то пригласил, поэтому третья форма: people invited (= who were invited).

stem.en: ___ by the noise, the baby started to cry.

why.en: The noise frightened the baby (passive meaning), so we use the past participle: Frightened.
why.uz: Shovqin chaqaloqni qoʻrqitdi (majhul maʼno), shuning uchun uchinchi shakl: Frightened.
why.ru: Шум напугал ребёнка (пассивное значение), поэтому третья форма: Frightened.

stem.en: Not ___ what to say, she just smiled.

why.en: A negative participle clause gives a reason: Not knowing = because she didn't know.
why.uz: Inkor sifatdosh oborot sababni bildiradi: Not knowing = because she didn't know.
why.ru: Отрицательный причастный оборот выражает причину: Not knowing = because she didn't know.

stem.en: It took me months to get used to ___ up at 5 a.m.

why.en: In get used to, to is a preposition, so the next verb takes -ing: getting up.
why.uz: Get used to da to — predlog, shuning uchun keyingi feʼl -ing oladi: getting up.
why.ru: В get used to частица to — предлог, поэтому следующий глагол с -ing: getting up.

stem.en: Don't worry about the noise. You'll soon ___ it.

why.en: Becoming familiar with something new is get used to + noun.
why.uz: Yangi narsaga asta-sekin koʻnikish get used to + ot bilan ifodalanadi.
why.ru: Постепенно привыкнуть к чему-то новому: get used to + существительное.

stem.en: My father ___ working at night, so he doesn't mind it.

why.en: Be used to + -ing means something is normal for you now: he is used to working.
why.uz: Be used to + -ing biror narsa hozir siz uchun odatiy ekanini bildiradi: he is used to working.
why.ru: Be used to + -ing — что-то стало для вас привычным: he is used to working.

I'm not used to eat so late.
I don't used to eating so late.
I'm not use to eating so late.

why.en: Be used to is followed by -ing, and used keeps its -d: I'm not used to eating.
why.uz: Be used to dan keyin -ing keladi, used esa -d bilan yoziladi: I'm not used to eating.
why.ru: После be used to идёт -ing, а used пишется с -d: I'm not used to eating.
